prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 131px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 231px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 209px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 95px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 908px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 620px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 619px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 620px (different strategies, not small variations).

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A crop-by-crop reference table for comparing sowing windows, harvest windows, yield, and notes across crops.","reading":"Readers anchor on the crop name in column 1, compare the paired sowing and harvest windows in columns 2–3, then check the short yield value and read remarks. Rows should remain readable as units, so wrapping in long date phrases and remarks must not make the schedule hard to scan.","groups":["Columns 2–3: বপন and কাটা are the paired temporal comparison and should have related widths and rhythm.","Columns 4–5: both are outcomes after the schedule, but column 4 is a short numeric value while column 5 is long free text, so they should not share a width."],"keep_intact":["Crop names and parenthetical variety identifiers such as বোরো ধান (উফশী)","Individual Bengali words; never break mid-word","Numeric yield values and the unit টন/হেক্টর"],"may_wrap":["Remarks prose in column 5","Multiword sowing and harvest date windows at spaces","Column headers, especially ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)","Crop labels only between words, not inside a word"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[100,145,135,65,174],"idea":"Balance the row label, paired date windows, and long remarks so no single column dominates and rows remain readable."},{"name":"B","widths":[95,170,155,60,139],"idea":"Give the paired sowing and harvest columns the widest share so the schedule can be compared at a glance, accepting a tighter remarks column."},{"name":"C","widths":[85,125,115,60,234],"idea":"Let the long remarks drive the layout, compressing the schedule columns toward their unbreakable-word minimum and giving the remaining width to comments."}]}
